newsitem.title: GREECE: INJURED AUSTRIAN TOURISTS TO BE FLOWN HOME.
newsitem.headline: INJURED AUSTRIAN TOURISTS TO BE FLOWN HOME.

text.p: A 17-year-old girl and her mother are among the victims of a fatal car crash on the Greek holiday island of Rhodes, Greek police said on Thursday.

Sylvia Bergsmann and her mother Kornelia were among five Austrian tourists killed on Wednesday when their minibus collided head-on with a pick-up truck on its way back from a day-trip to the ancient site of Lindos, 55km from Rhodes town.

Another five tourists - including Bergsmann's father and seven-year-old sister - were seriously injured in the accident and were transferred by a Hellenic Air Force C-130 airplane to Athens hospitals on Wednesday night.
The Austrian embassy in Athens said it was conferring with doctors on whether they could airlift the injured to Austria.
"We are looking at whether they can be moved today," Austrian ambassador Hans Sabaditsch told Reuters. He said the transfer would be carried out by ambulance airplane.

Sabaditsch said two of the tourists were in "not very good condition" but said seven-year-old Julia Bergsmann was in "pretty good shape for the circumstances". He gave no details on the condition of Bergsmann's father Alfred. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
